overview: The City Council approved a fuel storage license for a proposed BJ's Wholesale Club gas station subject to detailed neighborhood conditions following a court remand, heard an extensive presentation from municipal labor representatives regarding stalled contract negotiations, and approved multiple Community Preservation Act project funding requests.

items.title: Public Participation on City Labor Contract Negotiations
items.summary: Teamsters Local 25 Secretary-Treasurer Steven South reported that eight bargaining units representing municipal and school employees have worked years without wage increases and face city contract offers limited to 2 percent alongside benefit concessions, prompting councilors to voice support for the workers and frustration with city administration.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Moment of Silence Resolutions
items.summary: The council observed moments of silence honoring late Governor's Councilor Michael J. Callahan, late Senate President Thomas Birmingham, and late disability advocate Tom Aniletto, and adopted a resolution wishing John Granara a happy 80th birthday.

items.title: Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: The council tabled the meeting records from January 17, 2023, and approved committee reports covering proposed amendments to the Community Preservation Committee ordinance and recommended CPA projects.

items.title: Hearing 21-301: BJ's Wholesale Club Fuel Storage License
items.summary: Approved a remanded application by BJ's Wholesale Club for a flammable storage license to construct a gas station at 278 Middlesex Avenue, imposing 14 conditions addressing parking maintenance, landscaping, speed tables, electric vehicle chargers, and truck restrictions.

items.title: Petition 23-029: Common Victualler License for Daily Mart
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license petition submitted by Vimal Patel for Daily Mart at 267 Spring Street.

items.title: Hearing 22-412: Starbucks Special Permit for Extended Hours
items.summary: Approved a special permit allowing Starbucks Coffee at 177 College Avenue to operate extended morning hours from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m. daily, conditioned on the permit remaining with the business rather than the property.

items.title: Resolution 23-023: Green Stretch Energy Code Draft Language
items.summary: Adopted a resolution requesting that the Office of Planning, Development and Sustainability provide language to the council to adopt the specialized municipal opt-in green building code.

items.title: Resolution 23-024: MBTA Bus Network Redesign and Fare Policy Communication
items.summary: Adopted an amended resolution requesting the city administration and the MBTA inform residents about the transfer policy allowing two bus trips and one subway trip on a single fare, while urging the MBTA to maintain consistent public feedback channels.

items.title: Resolution 23-025: Discussion on Fire Fleet and Human Resources Concerns
items.summary: Approved an amended motion requesting that administration officials, human resources, and Medford Fire Department representatives attend the next meeting to discuss fire equipment status and employee health insurance access.

items.title: Resolution 23-026: City Census Mailing and 2022 Election Review
items.summary: Adopted an amended resolution urging communication on census form delivery amidst postal delays, inquiring whether vote-by-mail postcards will be sent to all residents in 2023, and requesting the elections manager present the 2022 elections after-action report.

items.title: Resolution 23-027: Inflation Reduction Act Clean Energy Tax Credits
items.summary: Adopted a resolution asking the administration to inform residents about clean energy tax credits and rebates available under the federal Inflation Reduction Act.

items.title: Resolution 22-028: Repainting Street Lines on Winthrop Street
items.summary: Adopted an amended resolution asking the administration and Eversource to repaint faded road lines, install lighting at speed tables on Winthrop Street, and repaint a crosswalk at Harvard Avenue and High Street.

items.title: Paper 22-519: Amendments to the Community Preservation Committee Ordinance
items.summary: Approved for first reading amendments to the municipal Community Preservation Committee ordinance concerning vacancies and project re-application timelines.

items.title: Paper 23-018: Community Preservation Committee Funding Appropriations
items.summary: Approved the mayor's request appropriating Community Preservation Act funds for eleven recommended projects, including $500,000 for the McGlynn playground, $402,000 for Carr Park pickleball courts, and $150,000 for Shiloh Baptist Church exterior restoration.

items.title: Resolutions 23-031 and 23-030: Off-Leash Dog Enforcement and Krystle Campbell Fountain Status
items.summary: Approved resolutions requesting code enforcement for off-leash dogs at Harris Park and asking the administration for an accounting of dedicated maintenance funds and repair status for the Krystle Campbell Peace Garden fountain.

items.title: Paper 23-017: Home Rule Petition for Institutional Master Plan Review
items.summary: Approved a home rule petition authorizing the municipality to review and approve institutional master plans.
